- **YoY-quarter decline** (Q4FY26 ~12% below Q4FY25) — volume moderation vs prior year; mgmt downplays as "aberration."

bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
- Confident, disciplined, conservative on guidance (insists on annual-not-quarterly framing; resets margin expectation *down* to 25–26% despite delivering 30%+ — under-promise posture).
- Transparent on cost pressures and pass-through mechanics; candid that defence is de-emphasised and that data-centers are irrelevant to its product (refreshingly non-hype).
- Accepts investor suggestion to add sector/geo revenue disclosure from Q1FY27 — responsive on governance/disclosure.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The "20% growth" is **volume**, not value — value growth could differ given price pass-throughs; investors conflating the two may over/under-estimate revenue.
- Management actively **cooled the data-center narrative** that a large client had stoked — signals candour but also caps a speculative re-rating angle.
- The ">₹100 cr PAT FY27" and "double sales by FY29 (~₹860 cr)" are explicitly **aspirations**, not guidance — and the ₹860 cr is achievable *within present capacity* (heavy operating leverage if utilisation climbs from ~63% toward full).
- Capex pulled forward to July despite sub-75% utilisation = early-cycle conviction signal on demand.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Deck explicitly lists debt-free status as a moat; finance costs were negligible at Rs 0.3 crore in FY26 versus Rs 0.7 crore in FY25.
- The ~Rs 120 crore greenfield capex is being funded off this debt-free balance sheet and phased over two years rather than in one hit.
- Returns profile cited at 28.6% RoCE and 22.0% RoE in FY26, down from the FY23 peak of 43.7% / 32.8% as the asset base and cash build.
- Capital is also being cycled into captive renewable generation, which converts capex into a recurring operating cost saving.

bull_bear.body:
- Over six decades of experience with strong metallurgical capabilities and expertise in complex, high-performance castings
- In-house engineering, pattern development and quality assurance systems supporting precision-engineered casting solutions
- Strong export orientation (~60% of turnover) across 16 countries, with customer stickiness from long OEM qualification cycles
- Robust product development engine — 144 new parts developed over the past three years, including 38 in FY26 — supporting future serial production visibility
- Debt-free balance sheet maintained for a third consecutive year, with free reserves of ~INR 114 Cr, enabling disciplined capital allocation and internal-accrual-funded growth

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Sectoral and industrial cyclicality — The Company's core end-markets (mining, construction equipment, railways, heavy engineering) are inherently cyclical and closely linked to global economic conditions and capital expenditure cycles; fluctuations in commodity demand, mining activity and infrastructure investment can influence order flows from OEM customers. Mitigated by maintaining a diversified sectoral presence and global customer base.
- Foreign exchange volatility — Given the Company's significant export orientation, movements in global currency markets can impact revenue realisations and margins; the Company monitors currency exposures and follows prudent financial practices to manage this.
- Raw material and energy price volatility — The foundry industry is exposed to volatility in steel scrap, alloys and power costs, which can influence production economics and margins; mitigated through efficient procurement, cost management and process improvement.
- Geopolitical developments and evolving trade dynamics — Ongoing geopolitical tensions, including conflicts affecting energy and logistics markets, may cause fluctuations in shipping costs, commodity prices and global demand patterns, requiring close engagement with customers and suppliers to ensure supply chain continuity.
- Tightening environmental regulation and carbon-related trade measures in export markets — Increasing focus on environmental regulations, sustainability standards and carbon emission controls (e.g., the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) requires continuous improvement in manufacturing processes and energy efficiency and may impact export competitiveness for high-carbon cast products.
- Customer concentration risk — The Company remains mindful of customer concentration risks given its OEM-focused, export-oriented business model.
- Supply chain disruption and technological change — The Company flags supply chain disruptions and technological changes as ongoing risk factors that require continuous monitoring within its structured risk management framework.
- Cyber security threats — The Company has implemented robust internal controls, information security systems and operational monitoring mechanisms to safeguard business operations and protect critical data and assets from cyber security threats.

outlook.body:
- **Revenue/volume growth:** ~**20%+ CAGR over next 3 years (through FY29), specifically FY27**. NOTE mgmt clarified the 20% refers to **volume growth**, not value.
- **Doubling aspiration:** Double volumes within *present capacity* → theoretically **~₹860 cr revenue by FY29** vs FY26 ₹423 cr.
- **PAT goal:** Aspiration to be a **">₹100 cr PAT company in FY27"** (could be ₹101cr or ₹115cr — framed as aspiration, not formal guidance; FY26 base ₹86.86 cr).
- **Margin:** Sustainable **EBITDA 25–26%** over the long term (may touch ~30% at times, but advised modelling 25–26%); historical band 28–30% EBITDA / 18–20% PAT.
- **Capacity utilisation:** FY26 ~**63–64%**; will NOT wait for 75% before adding capacity given strong customer indications.
- **Capex decision:** To be finalised by **end-July 2026** (advanced stage); originally contemplated for Dec-2026 but pulled forward. Project cost / size not yet disclosed.
- **GET contribution:** 1.1% of sales in FY26 → targeted **3.8% in FY27** (from existing customers).
- **Hybrid power:** 2.4 MW hybrid project commissioning by **June 2026**, ~₹3.6 cr/yr savings.

outlook.body:
- Expand global footprint (export presence in 16 countries, roadmap to 18) and deepen participation in international supply chains
- Enhance capacity utilisation as the product development pipeline transitions into serial production
- Progress further up the value chain through higher value-added offerings and sub-assemblies, increasing wallet share with existing customers
- Diversify sectoral exposure beyond mining and earthmoving into Ground Engaging Tools, construction, railways and defence to mitigate sector-specific cyclicality
- Strengthen relationships with global OEMs, expand presence across strategic markets and accelerate innovation

- Continue investing in product development (new parts pipeline) to build visibility for future serial production
- Pursue operational excellence via focused investments in technology, automation, digitisation and process optimisation

- Embed sustainability into long-term strategy, targeting carbon neutrality by FY 2029-30
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Steelcast's renewable-energy build-out continues to expand: the existing 4.5 MW Hybrid (Solar & Wind) Power Plant and the 5 MW Solar Power Plant (both commissioned in 2023) are running smoothly, and the Company is investing in a new 2.4 MW Hybrid (Solar & Wind) power plant under Group Captive mode, whose commissioning was pushed from 30th June 2026 to end-December 2026 due to operational difficulties. The Company is also further planning to set up a 1.5 MW Solar Power Project at the existing site of its Solar Power Plant, which together with the above would take total renewable power projects to 13.40 MW. Growth is being driven through 'utilisation-led expansion' of the existing Bhavnagar facility rather than new sites: management is targeting capacity utilisation of approximately 58% in FY 2026-27 and nearly 90% by FY 2028-29 (from ~48% currently), with capital expenditure tightly linked to reaching a 75% utilisation threshold before further expansion is undertaken. Alongside utilisation-led growth, the Company is investing in tooling and process capability to cut new-component development timelines from about 12 months to approximately 6-7 months, and is building readiness for fully machined/ready-to-use components (forward integration) to capture higher value addition. The Company also made capital investments of Rs. 89.01 Lakhs during FY 2025-26 on energy conservation equipment such as energy-efficient burners, air compressors and furnace revamping.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- China+1 sourcing shift continues to reshape global sourcing dynamics, positioning the Company as a preferred global partner as OEMs diversify away from China
- Structural demand from infrastructure development, mining activity and industrial capital expenditure across mining, earthmoving, construction, railways, cement/steel and defence sectors supports long-term visibility
- Diversified sectoral presence helps mitigate sector-specific cyclicality while supporting stable demand across domestic and export markets
- Tariff-related uncertainties, particularly in the U.S. market, are a headwind management is managing through pricing discipline and retention of its strategic supply-chain position
- Mining segment showing improvement versus FY25, with export demand in an uptrend and further improvement expected in FY27 supported by stronger commodity demand and gradual recovery in global mining activity
- Earthmoving equipment industry expected to maintain a positive outlook in FY27, supported by infrastructure development and construction activity; export demand expected to improve as global equipment inventories normalise
- Construction equipment sector continues steady growth on rising infrastructure and urban development investment, with strong indications seen late in FY26 expected to continue into FY27
- Railway/locomotive segment expected to show good signs in coming years following AAR certification and new parts development, despite a slight sales dip in FY26
- Ground Engaging Tools (GET) segment expected to see significant growth from new component development and customer-base expansion, including new US development orders and new Australian customers
- Raw material price volatility is managed through structured price variation mechanisms and diversified sourcing, supporting continuity and resilience
- EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) and evolving global trade policies flagged as an industry-level risk that may impact export competitiveness of high-carbon cast products
- Global supply chain realignments and India's relatively favourable trade relations with major economies continue to support export growth opportunities for Indian foundries such as Steelcast
- Robust product development pipeline (144 new parts developed over the past three years, including 38 in FY26) provides visibility for future serial production and supports higher capacity utilisation in coming years
- Management remains confident of sustaining a steady growth trajectory supported by a strong order pipeline and continued momentum in product development
- GET segment: new product development orders received from existing US customers and new customers developed in Australia, expected to support growth as new programs move into commercial production
- Railway segment: AAR certification in place along with new parts developed is expected to translate into good performance in the coming years

risks.note: The Company's core end-markets (mining, construction equipment, railways, heavy engineering) are inherently cyclical and closely linked to global economic conditions and capital expenditure cycles; fluctuations in commodity demand, mining activity and infrastructure investment can influence order flows from OEM customers. Mitigated by maintaining a diversified sectoral presence and global customer base.

Given the Company's significant export orientation, movements in global currency markets can impact revenue realisations and margins; the Company monitors currency exposures and follows prudent financial practices to manage this.

risks.risk: Raw material and energy price volatility
risks.note: The foundry industry is exposed to volatility in steel scrap, alloys and power costs, which can influence production economics and margins; mitigated through efficient procurement, cost management and process improvement.

risks.risk: Geopolitical developments and evolving trade dynamics
risks.note: Ongoing geopolitical tensions, including conflicts affecting energy and logistics markets, may cause fluctuations in shipping costs, commodity prices and global demand patterns, requiring close engagement with customers and suppliers to ensure supply chain continuity.

risks.risk: Tightening environmental regulation and carbon-related trade measures in export markets
risks.note: Increasing focus on environmental regulations, sustainability standards and carbon emission controls (e.g., the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) requires continuous improvement in manufacturing processes and energy efficiency and may impact export competitiveness for high-carbon cast products.
The Company remains mindful of customer concentration risks given its OEM-focused, export-oriented business model.

risks.risk: Supply chain disruption and technological change
risks.note: The Company flags supply chain disruptions and technological changes as ongoing risk factors that require continuous monitoring within its structured risk management framework.

The Company has implemented robust internal controls, information security systems and operational monitoring mechanisms to safeguard business operations and protect critical data and assets from cyber security threats.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Steelcast Limited manufactures specialised steel and alloy steel castings for Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) across heavy engineering sectors such as earthmoving and construction equipment, mining and mineral processing, steel and cement, and railways, where components must perform reliably under rigorous operating conditions. The product portfolio spans carbon steel, low alloy steel, high alloy steel and wear-resistant castings, manufactured using advanced No-Bake and Shell Moulding processes at an integrated facility in Bhavnagar, Gujarat, supported by in-house engineering, pattern development and quality assurance capabilities. The Company operates as a single reportable segment (Castings business only) under Ind AS 108.

one-line thesis: Debt-free, ~60%+ export steel-casting niche play riding global OEM outsourcing/China+1 with 30%+ EBITDA margins and a stated 20%+ volume CAGR aspiration to FY29 (double sales to ~₹860cr) plus a ">₹100cr PAT in FY27" goal — near-term margin wobble from fuel/freight/RM inflation is being passed through under cost-plus formulas.
financial scorecard:
**FY26 (YoY vs FY25):**
- Revenue from operations: **₹423.17 cr**, +13.33% YoY (FY25 ₹373.39 cr).
- EBITDA: **₹129.64 cr**, +17.30% YoY (FY25 ₹110.52 cr). **EBITDA margin 30.64%**, +104 bps (FY25 29.60%).
- PAT: **₹86.86 cr**, +20.31% YoY (FY25 ₹72.20 cr). **PAT margin 20.53%**, +119 bps (FY25 19.34%).

**Q4FY26 (QoQ vs Q3FY26):**
- Revenue: **₹112.43 cr**, +15.43% QoQ (Q3 ₹97.40 cr).
- EBITDA: **₹34.25 cr**, +9.74% QoQ (Q3 ₹31.21 cr). Implied Q4 EBITDA margin ~30.5%.
- PAT: **₹23.18 cr**, +12.58% QoQ (Q3 ₹20.59 cr). Implied Q4 PAT margin ~20.6%.
- Note: Q4FY26 was ~12% *below* Q4FY25 (mgmt called the YoY-quarter dip "an aberration"; volumes moderated vs prior-year quarter but improved sequentially).

**Balance sheet / cash:** Debt-free. Cash reserves **~₹114 cr**. Equity capital ~₹10.1 cr; ~16,000 shareholders.
**Order book:** ~₹130–135 cr as of 1-Apr-2026 (cycle ~110–120 days).
**One-offs / cost pressures (Q4):** Higher maintenance & machinery repairs; provisions for export-related obligations; higher fuel/power & energy costs (production ramp + fuel prices). RM cost up ~10% across the board from ~1-Mar-2026 (~4–5% sales-price impact), partly compensated from 1-Apr, balance expected from 1-Jul.
guidance (critical):
- **Revenue/volume growth:** ~**20%+ CAGR over next 3 years (through FY29), specifically FY27**. NOTE mgmt clarified the 20% refers to **volume growth**, not value.
- **Doubling aspiration:** Double volumes within *present capacity* → theoretically **~₹860 cr revenue by FY29** vs FY26 ₹423 cr.
- **PAT goal:** Aspiration to be a **">₹100 cr PAT company in FY27"** (could be ₹101cr or ₹115cr — framed as aspiration, not formal guidance; FY26 base ₹86.86 cr).
- **Margin:** Sustainable **EBITDA 25–26%** over the long term (may touch ~30% at times, but advised modelling 25–26%); historical band 28–30% EBITDA / 18–20% PAT.
- **Capacity utilisation:** FY26 ~**63–64%**; will NOT wait for 75% before adding capacity given strong customer indications.
- **Capex decision:** To be finalised by **end-July 2026** (advanced stage); originally contemplated for Dec-2026 but pulled forward. Project cost / size not yet disclosed.
- **GET contribution:** 1.1% of sales in FY26 → targeted **3.8% in FY27** (from existing customers).
- **Hybrid power:** 2.4 MW hybrid project commissioning by **June 2026**, ~₹3.6 cr/yr savings.
order book & pipeline:
- Opening order book ~**₹130–135 cr** as of 1-Apr-2026; conversion cycle ~110–120 days (roughly one quarter's revenue visibility).
- **50+ new parts** under various development stages (constant pipeline); approval pace *rose* in last 4–6 weeks despite geopolitics. New-part flow spans full 5 kg–2,500 kg weight range.
- Overseas **defence repeat order**: prototypes approved (compact vehicles for ground wars), awaiting serial-supply orders (delayed by Iran-U.S. situation); potential **₹15–18 cr** sales if it converts.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- Standalone business; no subsidiaries discussed.
- Core end-markets: **mining, earthmoving, construction, locomotives/railroad, ground engaging tools.** These five are the stated growth engines.
- **Railroad/locomotive:** certain critical components still "under stress" — developments not yet fully resolved; competitive intensity in railroad less favourable than the other segments, so focus tilted to mining/earthmoving/construction.
- **Exports >60% of revenue** (FY26); steady traction from North America & developed markets via OEM supply-chain diversification.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **China+1 / OEM outsourcing** — primary structural driver; global OEMs increasingly outsourcing specialised high-performance castings.
- **Ground Engaging Tools (GET)** — scaling 1.1%→3.8% of sales into FY27; optionality to grow further.
- **Overseas defence** — kept as opportunistic (₹15–18 cr potential), management has deliberately de-prioritised it.
- **Data centers — explicitly ruled out**: management says steel castings have practically no data-center application.
margins & cost dynamics:
- FY26 EBITDA margin 30.64% (+104 bps); near-term Q4 pressure from fuel/power, maintenance, export-obligation provisions.
- **Cost-plus / sales-price-variation formula** with all customers → RM/fuel cost increases passed through (auto formula, both directions). ~10% RM rise from Mar-1 → ~4–5% price pass-through; partial from Apr-1, balance from Jul-1.
- Rupee depreciation + >60% export mix act as natural cushions.
- Sustainable-margin frame reset lower (25–26% EBITDA) for conservative modelling despite recent 28–30%+ prints.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- Capacity-expansion capex decision **pulled forward from Dec-26 to end-July 2026** — currently "halfway through" the exercise; project cost and capacity quantum **NOT disclosed**. Watch for slippage past July and for actual size/cost when announced.
- 2.4 MW hybrid power project commissioning June-2026 (~₹3.6 cr/yr savings).
capital allocation:
- Debt-free balance sheet, ~₹114 cr cash — funding capex internally.
- **Bonus issue:** investor-prompted; management said "nothing on the horizon" but is "thinking" — no commitment.
- Dividend not specifically quantified on the call.
risks & watch-items:
- **YoY-quarter decline** (Q4FY26 ~12% below Q4FY25) — volume moderation vs prior year; mgmt downplays as "aberration."
- **Railroad component issues unresolved** — execution risk in one of the five target verticals.
- **Customer/geography concentration** historically a concern (investor flagged); diversification still in progress; no sector/geo revenue split disclosed yet (promised from Q1FY27).
- **Fuel/freight/RM inflation & Middle-East (Iran-U.S.) conflict** delaying orders (incl. defence) and raising costs; mitigated but not eliminated by cost-plus pass-through (lag) and FX.
- **Capex timing/sizing undisclosed** — execution and demand-visibility dependence.
- Cyclicality of end-user industries; FX exposure on >60% exports.
management quality / tone:
- Confident, disciplined, conservative on guidance (insists on annual-not-quarterly framing; resets margin expectation *down* to 25–26% despite delivering 30%+ — under-promise posture).
- Transparent on cost pressures and pass-through mechanics; candid that defence is de-emphasised and that data-centers are irrelevant to its product (refreshingly non-hype).
- Accepts investor suggestion to add sector/geo revenue disclosure from Q1FY27 — responsive on governance/disclosure.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The "20% growth" is **volume**, not value — value growth could differ given price pass-throughs; investors conflating the two may over/under-estimate revenue.
- Management actively **cooled the data-center narrative** that a large client had stoked — signals candour but also caps a speculative re-rating angle.
- The ">₹100 cr PAT FY27" and "double sales by FY29 (~₹860 cr)" are explicitly **aspirations**, not guidance — and the ₹860 cr is achievable *within present capacity* (heavy operating leverage if utilisation climbs from ~63% toward full).
- Capex pulled forward to July despite sub-75% utilisation = early-cycle conviction signal on demand.

themes.title: Railway rolling-stock & component capex
themes.need: A ~INR2.65 lakh cr Railways capital outlay and a pending ~1-lakh-wagon tender ('anytime this year' per JWL) drive rolling-stock, wheelsets, springs, castings, bogie components and interiors - with deep import-substitution (Neetu Yoshi 544434 castings; Airfloa 544516 interiors; Concord 543619 electronics). TITAGARH/TEXRAIL/JWL lead wagons; RVNL/IRCON/GPTINFRA on rail EPC.
themes.driver: Indian Railways large wagon tender award (next 1-2 quarters); wheelset plant ramp; Vande Bharat / Kavach orders.

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.
